mechanisms.title: Agent Note requirement, status lifecycle and supersession
mechanisms.problem: Repository decisions and non-obvious implementation rationale disappear from diffs, chat and commit messages; a generated note index adds conflict-prone aggregation; unmaintained or superseded notes become competing authorities.
triggers: The change makes or revises lasting decision rationale that code, tests and existing documentation cannot explain; mechanical/local edits, including local UI presentation and interaction, are exempt.
A decision is superseded, rejected, or no longer expected to guide future work.
A contributor or agent needs durable context that code and commit messages do not preserve.
obligations: Create or update the existing owning Agent Note only for lasting decision rationale; the archived 07-19 every-non-trivial-change rule is historical, not current authority.
State one explicit lifecycle status (proposed, implemented or rejected) and keep it aligned with reality.

Use the current lifecycle/class/date-topic path tree with checkable relative cross-links and no central generated index; connect the owned code/docs to its rationale without inventing a second note directory.
Keep the English and Chinese note bodies paired and update both when the decision changes.
When writing a new note, compare it with active notes covering the same decision, mechanism or rejected alternative and record full or partial supersession.

For complete implemented notes, delete purely mechanical/small-UI records as triplets with inbound-link repair; archive other historical-value records only when rationale no longer guides future work. Keep useful ownership, durable/wire, security, alternatives and reintroduction decisions active. Never archive proposed notes; keep rejected notes only while they prevent a plausible meaningful mistake.
Do not silently maintain archived history as current authority; link active prose to current owners instead.
steps: Decide whether durable rationale is missing from code, tests and existing docs; update the current owning note rather than duplicating it.
Use the lifecycle/class tree and required Problem, Decision/Proposal, Alternatives and Consequences/Acceptance/Risks skeleton appropriate to its status.
Write the paired Chinese body and let the pairing gate record the correspondence.
Link the note from affected code or documentation where the rationale is needed.
At decision change, update status and cross-link the superseding note; archive or delete only under the frozen-archive rules.
On every new note, search active notes for overlapping decisions and perform the scoped supersession check.

enforcement.mode: ci
enforcement.implementation: tools/agent-notes provides the executable classification, format and append-only archive checks; references/agent-notes.md routes target-cwd activation and trusted-baseline CI. Separate pairing/link gates and the named semantic-currency reviewer remain required.
enforcement.trust: Mechanical checks prove presence, pairing and archive integrity, not that prose still names the live mechanism; reviewers remain responsible for currency and correct supersession.
enforcement.failure: Missing lasting rationale is a review finding, not an automatic every-change note requirement. Classification, format, bilingual pairing and append-only archive-integrity failures must fail the activated documentation CI path; semantic currency and supersession remain reviewer responsibilities.
exceptions: Mechanical or local edits, including local UI presentation and interaction changes, may omit a note.
A rejected proposal may be deleted once it no longer prevents a plausible mistake.
Archived notes are intentionally frozen and may contain stale names and links.

mechanisms.applicability: Repositories with lasting decision rationale beyond code/tests/current docs. Activating the Note corpus also requires its classification/format/pairing and trusted-baseline archive checks; it is not permission to record every local change.
relationships: rationale-process-1-frozen-archive-integrity
rationale-process-1-bilingual-pairing-and-links
rationale-process-1-document-taxonomy-and-ownership

migration.strategy: Activate the current lasting-rationale policy together with mechanical classification/format/pairing and trusted-baseline archive gates; do not defer an existing source CI effect until corpus size justifies it.
migration.implementation: Use the shipped tools/agent-notes native executors and references/agent-notes.md for one lifecycle/class tree, format and trusted-baseline archive checks. Wire these into actual documentation/static CI together with the separate pairing/link gates; review semantic rationale and scoped supersession manually.
migration.requiredSupport: Executable classification, note-format, pairing and append-only archive validation; a trusted complete-history CI baseline; and an explicit reviewer checklist for semantic rationale/currency. These target checks must actually run before an enforcement claim.

positive.scenario: A decision with lasting rationale updates its existing owning note (or creates one if no owner exists), with the current lifecycle/class path, required sections, paired bodies and affected-code links.
positive.expected: The note is present, classified implemented or proposed, paired, and discoverable from the owned area.

positive.scenario: A new note fully supersedes an older implemented note; the old note is archived only after its rationale is captured and the active note name-checks it.
positive.expected: The active corpus has one current authority and archive history remains frozen and linkable.

rejection.scenario: A change introduces lasting rationale absent from code/tests/current docs but supplies only a commit message; contrast a local UI edit that needs no new decision note.
rejection.expected: Review rejects the change or requires a note; no automated semantic checker is claimed.

rejection.scenario: A proposed note is moved into the archive without becoming implemented.
rejection.expected: The archive verifier and review reject the move; proposed notes stay in the proposed lifecycle.

rejection.scenario: A note's English body is edited without the Chinese body.
rejection.expected: The pairing gate fails and the note is not accepted.

recovery.scenario: An archived note is found to contain a stale package name; a reader follows a link and needs current behavior.
recovery.expected: Current code and active documentation are consulted; the archived note is treated as history and is not rewritten.

recovery.scenario: A note is found to be superseded after landing.
recovery.expected: The author adds the supersession link, archives qualifying implemented history, and leaves partial supersession active and cross-linked.

limitations: Semantic currency is not mechanically proven; gates can pass while prose names a removed mechanism.
Archived notes intentionally freeze stale facts and links.
The source does not define a universal note-length or every-note coverage threshold.
mechanisms.status: Current lasting-rationale policy from AGENTS/README; the broader archived trigger is historical. Source mechanical CI gates exist; target execution must be separately evidenced.

mechanisms.title: Frozen Agent Note archive with sealed manifest
mechanisms.problem: Deleting every low-value implemented record erases historical evidence, while retaining every rejected proposal keeps implausible or unhelpful ideas in the active corpus. Relocated history can silently drift or lose files.
triggers: An implemented note's decision is complete and its rationale is unlikely to guide future work.
An archived artifact must be located, linked or audited.
A branch adds, moves or modifies files under the archive.
obligations: Admit only complete implemented triplets (English, Chinese, consistency sidecar) with the same valid archive date in both bodies, no earlier than the note filename date; the archive date need not equal creation date. Never archive proposed notes.

Move the complete triplet, retain Status: implemented and add Archived: YYYY-MM-DD in both languages; only relocation, that metadata line, sidecar re-record and mechanical inbound-link repair are permitted.
Freeze archived bytes: no later updates for renamed packages, behavior, translation standards, formatting, broken outbound links or later document contracts.

Exclude archive sources from ordinary format, translation-pairing, wrapping, Markdown-link, package-path, Mermaid, documentation-TypeScript and type-equivalence gates; validate links INTO archived files instead.
Seal each archived artifact by path and SHA-256 in an append-only manifest; --write first proves every existing seal unchanged, then appends only newly archived artifacts.
In PR CI, obtain a trusted base SHA and check out complete history so a reused runner's shallow checkout cannot omit the baseline manifest.
steps: Confirm the candidate is an implemented, complete triplet with lasting historical value and no expected future guidance role.
Move the triplet to .agents/notes/archived/<kind>/ with no redundant implemented segment; add the Archived line in both bodies; re-record the sidecar.
Repair inbound links mechanically and redirect readers to current authority where needed.
Run the archive verifier in write mode to prove prior seals then append new ones; commit manifest and files together.
In CI, run the verifier against the trusted base with full history and let ordinary gates skip archive sources.

enforcement.mode: ci
enforcement.implementation: tools/agent-notes/verify-archived-agent-notes.mjs supplies archive path/kind/date/triplet and Git-blob sidecar checks plus append-only SHA-256 seals. references/agent-notes.md specifies trusted base SHA and full-history target CI; providing the program is not proof that target protection runs it.
enforcement.trust: The manifest proves byte identity and append-only behavior; it does not prove that the archived decision was wise or that its links remain useful.
enforcement.failure: A modified or missing archived byte, a malformed triplet, an invalid date or an unreachable baseline fails the verifier; ordinary gates exclude the archive.
exceptions: Mechanical inbound-link edits to active prose are allowed and are not archive-source edits.

The source's exact historical Figma seal transitions authorize only that source repository. The migrated executor does not transfer them or offer a general unseal flag; any target historical correction needs separate explicit trusted authorization and an exact audited process.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects that need durable historical decisions without letting history pose as current authority. Requires Git history and a stable archive path.
relationships: archive is a lifecycle terminus for implemented notes
archive sidecars are excluded from ordinary pairing but are sealed by the archive verifier

migration.strategy: Create the archive path, freeze rules and manifest verifier before moving the first note.
migration.implementation: Adopt the shipped tools/agent-notes/verify-archived-agent-notes.mjs and references/agent-notes.md, target-owned archive instructions, complete triplets, Git-blob sidecars, SHA-256 seals, trusted-baseline CI and a search exclusion for archived history.
migration.requiredSupport: Native Node ESM executor, target Git object access and a trusted complete-history CI baseline; execute default read-only verification or explicit --write append locally, and configure ordinary documentation gates to exclude archive sources.

positive.scenario: An implemented note is archived with its Chinese body and sidecar; the verifier writes and later verifies an appended seal with the correct date and hashes.
positive.expected: The archive contains one complete triplet, the manifest has one new sealed entry, and active gates still pass.

rejection.scenario: An archived file is edited after sealing, or a proposed note is archived.
rejection.expected: The verifier fails on the changed hash or lifecycle; the file is restored or returned to the proposed corpus.

rejection.scenario: A shallow CI checkout lacks the baseline manifest.
rejection.expected: The verifier refuses to treat the truncated history as a valid baseline; CI must fetch the trusted base and full history.

recovery.scenario: A moved note leaves broken inbound links.
recovery.expected: Active prose is repaired or redirected; the archived bytes stay unchanged and remain citable as history.

limitations: Archived facts and outbound links may be stale by design.
The manifest guarantees integrity, not semantic adequacy.
A partial checkout can invalidate the baseline proof; the source requires explicit CI configuration.
mechanisms.status: current; archive verifier and seal implemented

mechanisms.title: Mechanical quality gates and evidence chains
mechanisms.problem: Prose instructions and code review alone do not reliably preserve repository invariants; checks can drift between local and CI, be skipped, report only success, or capture evidence that cannot be re-verified. Broad suppressions can hide rules without addressing the underlying problem.
triggers: An invariant is important enough that a reviewer could miss it or a contributor could reasonably forget it.
A check is added, removed, or moved between local hooks, scripts and CI.
A visual, runtime or generated artifact is used as review evidence.
A gate exception, baseline or suppression is proposed.
obligations: Encode important repository promises as executable checks that fail on violation; do not rely on reviewer memory alone.

Keep local and CI on the same executable gate implementation, but run explicit local and CI profiles: hooks spend their latency budget on cheap local defects, while CI runs the exhaustive set and owns the final verdict. The archived note's hook/CI symmetry is superseded by the later fast-local-git-hooks decision; CI as the exhaustive enforcement path remains current. Make the required CI result depend on the checks rather than on an advisory report.

Run independent checks so one run reports all independent failures; use fail-fast only where the source defines it, terminate the whole process tree on the first blocking failure, record not-yet-run and killed-but-zero-exit gates as skipped (never passed), and keep advisory diagnostic lanes complete. Never record unfinished work as passed.
Every claimed verification has positive, rejection and recovery evidence; a green summary or a historical replay is not sufficient.

Capture browser/runtime evidence through one causal execution chain: pin an exact clean-worktree commit, use fresh application/workspace/session/browser state, keep every published frame from the same server and model-backed run, discard failed runs, wait for unique semantic states, and add detail/trajectory frames for tool calls, rejections and recovery. The final encoded GIF is the verification subject; decode frames from it rather than substituting source screenshots. Re-read the live PR body and verify the uploaded URL (or assets-branch path, bytes, checksum, status and media type); a successful upload or push is not evidence.
Gate exceptions must be narrow, justified and mechanically bounded; prefer exact baselines over file-wide allowances or count budgets.
Remove a check only after its permanent replacement is active; do not leave a second apparent enforcement path.

Prefer the available browser-control workflow; if unavailable, use the repository-declared Playwright in an isolated headless browser, not a new driver or the user's browser. A native production surface may be replaced only through normal configuration with an official browser-operable production backend, stated beside the GIF; fixtures, mock transports, synthetic events and test-only hooks do not substantiate a real-production claim.
steps: State the invariant and the observable failure it prevents.
Implement the check as a deterministic command over tracked inputs, with a clear failure message and remedy.
Wire the gate into explicit local and CI profiles with their intended subsets, and add positive/rejection/recovery tests for the gate itself.
Record exact exceptions with fingerprints or per-item baselines; provide a prune operation that refuses to add exceptions.
For runtime evidence, pin the exact head, use fresh isolated state, run once, capture and verify the final artifact, and re-read the publication boundary; do not combine frames from separate runs.
Audit and remove obsolete gates only after replacement verification.

enforcement.mode: mostly automatic CI plus review for semantic scope
enforcement.implementation: Executable scripts, gate runner with dependency graph and process-tree termination, required CI jobs, exact baselines, artifact verification, tests for the checks themselves
enforcement.trust: A passing check proves only its encoded predicate over the inputs it actually read; a failing checker is not proof that a forge blocks the merge, and a green aggregate can hide advisory diagnostics. The source archive explicitly supersedes the hook/CI symmetry; do not claim identical local and CI coverage unless the target adopts and verifies it.
enforcement.failure: A failed or skipped required step exits nonzero and blocks completion; missing evidence is treated as unverified; exceptions fail closed when stale or unlisted.
exceptions: Advisory diagnostics may be outside the required verdict only when explicitly labeled and visible.
Exact historical baselines may permit known debt with no command that adds new debt.
Checks may be removed only after a replacement owns the invariant.

mechanisms.applicability: Any project with repeatable invariants and a CI system. The source mechanisms scale down to a single local script if the same verify/fail/recover behavior is preserved.
relationships: must preserve the same outputs and diagnostics while reducing work
an exact-baseline example
defines the review evidence and scope report that complement gates

migration.strategy: Start with the highest-risk invariant, make one executable check, and wire it to both local and required CI.
migration.implementation: Create a gate runner or use an existing one; add dependency-aware scheduling, buffered failure output, fail-fast where needed, positive/rejection/recovery tests, and an exception ledger with prune-only semantics.
migration.requiredSupport: A deterministic test environment, a CI required-check configuration the team controls, and a review process that does not treat a green summary as complete evidence.

positive.scenario: A gate is wired to the local profile and required CI; a violating change produces a nonzero exit, a named failure and a remedy message.
positive.expected: The required verdict is red, the failure identifies the input, and independent gates still report their own results.

positive.scenario: A browser evidence report links the raw capture and the command that re-verifies it; an independent reviewer reproduces the same result.
positive.expected: The evidence chain has one execution and a real re-verification path, not a derived thumbnail.

rejection.scenario: A check is skipped because a local hook was bypassed.
rejection.expected: Required CI still runs the same command; the bypass does not produce a green required result.

rejection.scenario: A new suppression or file-wide allowance is proposed for a baseline gate.
rejection.expected: Review rejects it; only exact per-item entries or decreased counts are accepted.

rejection.scenario: A failing advisory job is shown while the aggregate is green.
rejection.expected: The aggregate does not claim the advisory check passed; failure remains visible in the run summary.

recovery.scenario: A gate is found to be stale or superseded.
recovery.expected: Its owner either restores the invariant with a replacement check or records the removal and the new owner; no gap is silently declared.

recovery.scenario: A forged or ambiguous evidence artifact is found.
recovery.expected: The raw artifact is re-run or rejected; the report is corrected and the check is strengthened.

limitations: Checks prove only their encoded predicate; they do not prove prose meaning, design quality or human readiness.
CI configuration and forge blocking are external trust boundaries and require real evidence.
Exact baselines allow known debt and can become stale if pruning is neglected.

The main quality-gates note is archived; its hook/CI symmetry is superseded, and only the exhaustive CI role remains a current source obligation. Local hook parity is migration design, not a recovered current guarantee.
Per-file 100% coverage can be satisfied by assertion-free tests; mutation testing was only a planned counterweight in the source.
mechanisms.status: current with superseded local-hook symmetry; CI exhaustive role remains

mechanisms.title: Explicit change scope, concrete prose and decidable review
mechanisms.problem: Broad or vague changes hide what behavior moved, what was actually verified and which parts are speculation. Simplification surveys delete or retain code from impression rather than evidence. Abstract prose and ambiguous identifiers make review unverifiable, and piecemeal aliases preserve ambiguity.
triggers: A change spans several concerns, deletes code, or claims a cleanup or simplification.
A reviewer must decide whether a claim is supported by observed behavior, source or tests.
Prose or identifiers use a broad label whose meaning depends on context.
A pre-release public symbol or durable field needs renaming.
obligations: State the change scope explicitly: intended behavior, affected owners, what is verified, what is inferred, and what is out of scope.
Keep review units independently reviewable; do not mix an enforcement decision with unrelated bulk redesign.
For deletions and simplifications, survey evidence first: callers, runtime paths, tests, historical decisions and replacement ownership; report uncertainty rather than converting it into deletion.
Write concrete prose: name the actor, action, object and recorded fact; prefer the local exact concept over an abstract umbrella label.
Ban a token mechanically only when it has accumulated unrelated meanings; replace each occurrence with the local concept and keep sentence-level review for meaning.

Pre-release, prefer coordinated renames of public symbols and durable fields over aliases; a runtime compatibility reader may reconstruct a retired key without embedding the retired token in maintained text.
Review checklists must be decidable: each item names an observable artifact or failure, not an impression such as 'clean' or 'friendly'.
steps: Write the scope/evidence section before requesting review.
Classify each claim as source fact, observed execution, inference or migration design.
For a simplification, enumerate callers and tests, preserve behavior or record the intended change, then delete only with replacement ownership.
Replace ambiguous terms with local concepts; run the mechanical ban and review the replacement meaning.
Check every review item against a named artifact; reject claims that cannot be observed.
Record the resulting decision and residual uncertainty.

enforcement.mode: review plus targeted mechanical checks
enforcement.implementation: change-scope report, review checklist, evidence tables, concrete-prose review, optional token-ban scanner, tests updated with behavior
enforcement.trust: Mechanical scans prove token absence or syntax, not that the remaining prose is precise; scope reports are author claims until a reviewer checks the evidence.
enforcement.failure: Unsupported deletion or unverifiable claim is rejected; a banned token outside its exemptions fails the scan; an alias that preserves the ambiguity is rejected.
exceptions: Historical persistence evidence may retain selected identifiers inside generated/historical schema markers.
Archived and vendored sources may be excluded where their ownership rules forbid edits.
A broad term may remain when it names a genuinely single local concept and review records that meaning.

mechanisms.applicability: Any review process where scope, deletion or prose precision matters. The token-ban part applies only after a term has demonstrably accumulated unrelated meanings.
relationships: another syntax-level restriction with exact debt accounting
scope reports and review are evidence inputs, not substitutes for gates
concrete prose supports document content review

migration.strategy: Add a short scope/evidence section and a decidable checklist before adding scanners.
migration.implementation: Provide a PR template or note section for scope and evidence, define concrete prose review, inventory token ambiguity, then add a narrow scanner with documented exemptions and tests.
migration.requiredSupport: Reviewer time, a repository-wide search capability, and an exemption policy for historical/vendored content.

positive.scenario: A simplification PR lists callers, tests, preserved contracts and residual uncertainty; a reviewer reproduces the evidence and accepts the deletion.
positive.expected: The deletion has a named evidence basis and the review checklist items are observable.

positive.scenario: A pre-release rename changes public symbols and fixtures in one coordinated change; compatibility code reads the old durable key at runtime without embedding the retired token.
positive.expected: Maintained text contains the precise new concepts and no alias keeps both meanings alive.

rejection.scenario: A cleanup deletes a helper because a search found no textual references.
rejection.expected: Review rejects the deletion unless dynamic/registration paths and runtime behavior were checked.

rejection.scenario: A banned token is replaced with one broad synonym such as origin/source.
rejection.expected: The replacement is rejected as preserving ambiguity; each site must name its local concept.

rejection.scenario: A review item says only 'improve clarity'.
rejection.expected: The item is not decidable; it is rewritten to name an artifact, outcome or observable failure.

recovery.scenario: A token slips into an exempt historical area.
recovery.expected: The exemption is confirmed against the historical-schema boundary; current names and authored guidance remain checked.

recovery.scenario: A simplification later proves wrong.
recovery.expected: The evidence record and revision history identify what was missed; the change is reverted and the checklist is strengthened.

limitations: Scope reports and review checklists are still human judgments.
A mechanical token ban addresses one known ambiguous term, not general vague language.
Exemptions can hide current misuse if their boundary is not kept narrow.

mechanisms.title: Exact baseline against new unknown assertions
mechanisms.problem: An assertion through unknown removes TypeScript's compatibility check between the original value and the asserted type; production code can hide a wrong interface and tests can claim an incomplete fixture satisfies a service. A bulk cleanup would mix enforcement with unrelated type and fixture redesign.
triggers: First-party JavaScript or TypeScript adds as unknown or <unknown>, including tests, fixtures, benchmarks and scripts.
An existing assertion is edited, moved, renamed or deleted.
A baseline entry becomes stale or someone proposes a file-wide or count-based exception.
obligations: Prohibit new direct assertions to unknown in first-party JS/TS, including parenthesized target types and union targets with a direct unknown member.
Keep unknown declarations valid for external data that enters through an explicit parser boundary.
Record every existing assertion exactly: repository-relative path, SHA-256 digest of syntax tokens, occurrence count.
Allow baseline edits only to delete entries or decrease counts; reject added files, new fingerprints and increased counts.
Provide a prune command that refuses to write while new violations exist; provide no command that adds exceptions.
Run the checker from CI static/primary modes and local hygiene profiles.
steps: Parse tracked and non-ignored untracked source with the language syntax tree, ignoring comments, strings and declarations.
Compare each assertion's path+fingerprint+count against the exact baseline.
Fail on new, changed, unlisted or stale entries.
After genuinely removing a cast, run prune to delete or reduce its entry.
Route remaining assertions to their owners for type, parser or fixture fixes.

enforcement.mode: automatic syntax-tree check with an exact ratchet baseline
enforcement.implementation: TypeScript AST scan, SHA-256 token fingerprints, path+count ledger, prune-only write path, CI static/primary and local hygiene profiles
enforcement.trust: The check proves absence of unlisted direct unknown assertions, including union targets absorbed by a direct unknown member; it does not prove general type safety or resolve aliases/intersections.
enforcement.failure: A new or changed assertion and a stale baseline entry both fail; reviewers must reject added fingerprints or counts.
exceptions: Vendored sources and frozen archived Agent Notes retain ownership exclusions.
JavaScript JSDoc @type, unknown[], Promise<unknown> and other containing types are outside this syntactic rule.

mechanisms.applicability: TypeScript or JavaScript projects with existing unknown assertions and independent owners. It can be generalized to any syntax pattern with exact per-site debt.
relationships: an exact-baseline gate with prune-only exceptions
separates enforcement from unrelated cleanup

migration.strategy: Adopt exact existing debt and enforce only new assertions; clean up per owner.
migration.implementation: Implement the AST checker and baseline generator, wire it to required CI, document the prune-only rule, and add fixture tests for comments, strings, angle-bracket syntax and union targets.
migration.requiredSupport: Language parser, deterministic tracked-file enumeration, stable fingerprint format and review acceptance of the ratchet.

positive.scenario: A new as unknown in a test is added; the checker reports the path and fingerprint and exits nonzero.
positive.expected: Required CI blocks and the author replaces the assertion with a typed parser or fixture change.

positive.scenario: An existing cast is removed; prune deletes its entry and the check remains green.
positive.expected: The baseline shrinks and no obsolete allowance accumulates.

rejection.scenario: A file-wide allowance or whole-repository count is proposed.
rejection.expected: Review rejects it because a new assertion could replace a removed one.

rejection.scenario: A cast is hidden in a string/comment or uses angle-bracket syntax.
rejection.expected: The AST checker either ignores non-assertion text or detects the real assertion; a text-only search would be rejected as insufficient.

rejection.scenario: A baseline entry's fingerprint is manually relaxed.
rejection.expected: The ledger diff is rejected; only deletion or count decrease is accepted.

recovery.scenario: An operand identifier is renamed, invalidating the fingerprint.
recovery.expected: The author resolves the cast or updates its exact entry through the prune path; formatting-only whitespace/comment changes preserve the token fingerprint.

limitations: Does not establish type safety or resolve type aliases/intersections.
JSDoc and container types are outside the rule.
Replacing a cast with any, another unchecked assertion or a hiding helper does not solve the typing problem.

mechanisms.title: Graph-based work budgets, bounded hang guards and deterministic test teardown
mechanisms.problem: A wall-clock timeout measures runner speed rather than the work being asserted, so a slow host and a grown input are indistinguishable. Fixed sleeps and tight process-confirmation budgets fail under contention, and tests that create temporary roots leak inodes on shared runners.
triggers: A gate's pass/fail uses an elapsed-time threshold while its real assertion is about input size or placement.
A test waits a fixed duration for a fire-and-forget write, child exit, watcher event or dispose ladder.
A test or helper creates temporary directories on a shared host.
obligations: Decide growth with a structural work budget computed from the actual produced graph (for example packages per version times checked edges), not from a prediction or elapsed time.
Emit the measured counts, the budget and the instruction to measure and deliberately raise the constant when the budget is exceeded.
Keep a separate wall-clock hang guard derived from the work budget so a very slow runner cannot decide the gate's outcome; document its derivation.
Treat budget raising as a ratchet: it requires a fresh measurement and a deliberate constant change, not a timeout bump.
Replace fixed sleeps with an awaited observable completion or a bounded probe for the actual precondition; keep a real deadline so a genuine hang still fails.
Have every test remove the temporary roots it created at teardown, on success and failure, instead of relying on machine-side sweeps.
Do not convert a flaky but important suite into a permanently advisory check; repair determinism or record the limitation explicitly.
steps: Identify what the gate actually asserts and which structural counts bound that cost.
Compute the budget from the observed graph and add a derived hang guard.
On budget failure, measure the new resolution cost before changing the constant.
For timing-sensitive tests, replace fixed settle/budget values with awaited events or bounded readiness probes; keep the assertion.
Register every created temp root and delete it in afterEach/afterAll with recursive force removal.
Verify determinism under contention and record any remaining environment-dependent files.

enforcement.mode: automatic budget assertion plus test teardown
enforcement.implementation: assertResolutionWorkBudget-style structural check, derived NPM_HANG_GUARD_MS, deterministic waits, process-ready probes, temp-root registry and recursive cleanup
enforcement.trust: The budget proves the produced graph stays within a measured structural limit; it does not prove the gate cannot hang, and the hang guard still consumes the full bound before failing.
enforcement.failure: A graph above budget fails with counts and remedy; a missing budget measurement is rejected; leaked temp roots are a test defect; fixed-sleep assertions that flake remain failures.
exceptions: Product spill directories that follow a retention policy are not test temp dirs and may persist.
A bounded hang guard may be generous when it cannot influence the substantive verdict.

mechanisms.applicability: Gates whose cost scales with input size and tests that coordinate asynchronous or child-process behavior, especially on shared CI.
relationships: optimizations must not weaken determinism
budgets and teardown are part of the evidence contract
contended native runners expose these failures first

migration.strategy: Replace timeout verdicts with one structural budget and derive a separate hang guard; fix tests at their synchronization points.
migration.implementation: Expose the produced graph summary, add an assert function with measured counts, derive the guard, replace fixed sleeps with event/probe helpers, and add teardown that removes created roots.
migration.requiredSupport: A summary of the asserted graph, timing measurements on representative hosts, and test helpers for readiness and temp-root tracking.

positive.scenario: A dependency-layout lane adds packages and crosses the structural budget; the failure prints both counts and the budget, not only elapsed seconds.
positive.expected: The failure is deterministic across fast and slow runners and names the measured growth.

positive.scenario: A test that previously slept 40ms awaits the actual write-drain signal and passes under contention.
positive.expected: The assertion is unchanged and the flake disappears without a larger arbitrary sleep.

rejection.scenario: A maintainer raises the timeout to make a slow runner pass.
rejection.expected: Review rejects the change as leaving the runner-dependent verdict in place; a structural budget and hang guard are required.

rejection.scenario: A test creates a temp root and relies on a periodic sweep.
rejection.expected: Review rejects the sweep as a substitute for owning teardown; the test must remove its root.

rejection.scenario: A bounded process exit probe still fails under contention.
rejection.expected: The probe must observe the actual exit edge or record the platform limitation; a tight constant is not accepted as evidence of product failure.

recovery.scenario: The machine fills with temp residue.
recovery.expected: The producing tests are identified and fixed; a sweep may contain damage but does not replace teardown.

recovery.scenario: A genuine hang occurs under the new budget.
recovery.expected: The derived hang guard eventually fails the lane; the diagnostic distinguishes elapsed time from graph growth.

limitations: A structural budget can miss growth that changes graph shape without changing the chosen product.
The hang guard is intentionally generous and can consume its full bound.
Some environment-dependent files remain; they are recorded rather than claimed fixed.

mechanisms.title: Document tiers, budgets, package-anchored ownership and maintenance modes
mechanisms.problem: Without tiers and owners, the same fact is copied into guides, package docs and generated references; pages grow without budget discipline; subsystem pages drift from the packages they describe; proposals and living specifications are confused.
triggers: A new document, section or generated page is proposed.
A fact changes and multiple documents could claim it.
A package's public surface or subsystem boundary moves.
A document is a proposal, an RFC, or a current specification.
obligations: Assign each durable fact one owner by document tier and link other places to it instead of copying enums, paths or defaults.
Apply explicit word budgets per tier, with a target and a temporary ceiling; keep headroom and a ratchet rather than silently raising the ceiling.
Anchor subsystem pages to package/ownership layout so navigation follows the product and code structure.
Label the maintenance mode of each document (authored, generated, mixed, frozen, proposal) and do not ask readers to infer it.
Distinguish a proposal/RFC from a living specification; when the decision lands, update the living owner and retire or archive the proposal.
Keep generated relationship atlases derived from source metadata rather than hand-maintained link lists.
steps: Classify the document tier and maintenance mode before writing.
Find the single current owner of each fact; move or link rather than duplicate.
Check the tier budget target and available headroom; split or relocate when exceeded rather than only raising the ceiling.
Anchor subsystem content to packages and update navigation with the code move.
For a proposal, state its status and the condition for landing; move durable rules to the living owner when accepted.
Regenerate relationship indexes from source and verify freshness.

enforcement.mode: documentation review plus budget, link and generated-freshness checks
enforcement.implementation: tiered docs with budgets, package-anchored subsystem tree, maintenance-mode labels, generated atlas, pairing and link gates
enforcement.trust: Budget checks prove a ceiling, not that the target or headroom rule is respected; generated atlases prove source coverage, not reader comprehension.
enforcement.failure: A copied fact, missing owner, exceeded hard ceiling or unlabeled maintenance mode is a review finding; stale generated pages fail their check.
exceptions: Exhaustive generated references may exceed ordinary prose budgets when their entry layer and split rule are defined.
Frozen historical documents keep their original form.

mechanisms.applicability: Documentation sets large enough that duplication and ownership ambiguity cause real maintenance cost.
relationships: defines what each tier must contain
projects the same sources into the site
owns deterministic regeneration of catalogs

migration.strategy: Inventory existing documents, define tiers/owners and budgets, then migrate one topic at a time.
migration.implementation: Add a document index or frontmatter with tier and maintenance mode, set target/ceiling budgets, anchor subsystem pages to packages, and add a generated relationship atlas only when source metadata can drive it.
migration.requiredSupport: Agreed tier vocabulary, ownership mapping to packages, budget manifest and a link/navigation update path.

positive.scenario: A new subsystem page is added for a package; its owner, tier, maintenance mode and budget are recorded and links use the package anchor.
positive.expected: The page has one owner, stays within budget or records an approved exception, and the atlas reflects the source package.

positive.scenario: A proposal is accepted; its durable rules move to the living specification and the proposal is marked historical.
positive.expected: Current docs and proposal status do not compete as authority.

rejection.scenario: A fact is copied into a guide and a package README with no owner link.
rejection.expected: Review identifies the duplicate and requires one owner plus a link.

rejection.scenario: A page exceeds its ceiling and the author raises the ceiling without measuring headroom.
rejection.expected: The budget check or review rejects the silent ratchet; the page is split or the target is reconsidered.

rejection.scenario: A generated atlas is hand-edited.
rejection.expected: The next generation overwrites it or the freshness check fails; edits belong in source metadata.

recovery.scenario: A package move invalidates subsystem navigation.
recovery.expected: The anchor and atlas are updated with the code move; redirects or aliases preserve old routes where needed.

recovery.scenario: A budget target is stricter than the content warrants.
recovery.expected: The owner records the measured exception and adjusts the target with review, rather than deleting required behavior.

limitations: Budget ceilings do not prove the target or headroom rule.
Tier assignment remains a judgment that can be gamed.
Generated relationship coverage does not prove the relationships are meaningful.

mechanisms.title: Bilingual pairing, section records and localized link integrity
mechanisms.problem: Bilingual documents diverge or silently present one language as canonical; merge conflicts occur on a shared record even when both language files merge cleanly; GitHub resolves links without the site locale projector, so a shared target sends Chinese readers to English pages; source-discovery gaps let broken index links escape the checker.
triggers: A document has an English and a Chinese body, or is proposed for translation.
A section is edited on one side or two branches edit different sections.
A link target belongs to the bilingual corpus.
A new document class or index file may fall outside the link checker's discovery.
obligations: Maintain equal authority for both languages; neither is canonical. Keep a consistency record with enough information to detect content-only divergence and support same-PR edits.
Prefer per-heading section records over whole-file blob hashes so independent section edits do not force a record conflict, and compute hashes from normalized content.
Keep the record merge-safe and machine-generated; a worktree-local merge driver does not help GitHub mergeability, so do not rely on one for PR merge.
For every discovered non-excluded source, require a complete pair, matching switchers except documented generated English, and an identical structural signature.

Resolve in-repository document links to the target in the source file's locale: English to .md, Chinese to .zh.md; preserve the same semantic target and query/fragment; a missing counterpart in the corpus is a pairing error, not a fallback.

Check relative-path targets only (skip schemes, protocol-relative, root-absolute and pure fragments), strip query/fragment, resolve against the linking directory, and fail nonzero on the first broken link.
Include every source class that can contain an in-scope link, including root/package index files; test the same discovery function the command uses.
steps: Author both language bodies and the consistency record; run the pairing writer explicitly so the record diff is reviewable.
On edit, update the counterpart and re-record the changed section rather than the whole file.
Select link targets by the source document's locale and keep the same semantic target and suffix in both sides.
Run the link checker over the full discovery scope, including index files, and fix the link rather than weakening the gate.
For a move, preserve redirects or update both sides and the record.

enforcement.mode: automatic linking and pairing gates in doc-sync/CI
enforcement.implementation: section-keyed i18n sidecars with hashes, pairing writer/verifier, structural signatures, locale-aware relative-link resolution, mdast/GFM checker with explicit discovery, symlink dedup
enforcement.trust: The gates prove complete pairs, consistent section hashes, matching structure and existing relative targets; they do not prove the translation is accurate or that archived/generated content is covered.
enforcement.failure: An incomplete pair, changed section without re-record, mismatched structural signature, broken relative target or invalid switcher fails the gate; the checker reports the path and first broken link.
exceptions: Generated English-only references, instruction-only files and bilingual-by-construction files may be excluded by an explicit manifest.
External URLs, images, pure fragments and out-of-scope targets keep their existing behavior.
Archived notes are excluded from ordinary pairing and link-source checks.

mechanisms.applicability: Any documentation set with maintained translations and in-repository cross-links, especially if a site projector masks source-level link differences.
relationships: defines which documents are in the bilingual corpus
the site must not hide source-level link errors
notes are part of the paired corpus unless excluded

migration.strategy: Introduce paired files with a sidecar and one gate, then make links locale-aware and close discovery gaps.
migration.implementation: Create the pair convention, writer/verifier, structural signature and exclusion manifest; add locale-aware link resolution and a single shared discovery function for the checker and its tests.
migration.requiredSupport: A stable hash format, merge-safe record format or merge driver, HTML/Markdown parser, and a review process for translation quality.

positive.scenario: A section is edited in English; the author updates Chinese and re-records the section; two branches editing different sections merge without a record conflict.
positive.expected: The pair is consistent and the record contains independent section hashes.

positive.scenario: A Chinese page links to a page that has a reviewed Chinese counterpart; the href points to .zh.md and preserves the fragment.
positive.expected: GitHub and the site route to the same localized target; the link check passes.

rejection.scenario: Only the English body changes, leaving the record stale.
rejection.expected: The pairing gate fails on the section hash; the author updates both sides and re-records.

rejection.scenario: A broken link exists in packages/README.md.
rejection.expected: The shared discovery function includes the index and the checker fails; a one-off repair without fixing discovery is rejected.

rejection.scenario: A Chinese link targets .md while a .zh.md counterpart exists.
rejection.expected: The localization rule rejects the link as a pair-completeness error.

recovery.scenario: The consistency record conflicts on a shared blob line.
recovery.expected: The section-keyed format or a local merge plus re-record resolves it; the PR is not accepted with a stale record.

recovery.scenario: A link target moves.
recovery.expected: Both sides, the record and any redirect/alias are updated; the gate verifies the new target.

limitations: Gates prove pairing and link existence, not translation quality or semantic equivalence.
Per-section records still conflict when the same section changes on two branches.
GitHub mergeability does not run worktree-local merge drivers.

mechanisms.title: Single-source documentation projection, raw twins and self-contained assets
mechanisms.problem: A documentation site can silently become a second copy of the corpus, its navigation can drift from the source manifest, rendered pages can still carry repository-only chrome, agents can be forced to scrape HTML, and images can depend on the source checkout or remote hosts.
triggers: A canonical Markdown document is published to a website.
Navigation, section order or route manifests change.
An agent or external consumer needs the source Markdown rather than rendered HTML.
A page references an image or another document.
obligations: Project canonical Markdown into the site; do not maintain a second authored copy.
Own section placement and navigation order in one source (for example website/docs.ts); throw on a locale group with no declared placement rather than falling back to sort order.
Make route and manifest publication agree; a nav item whose route does not exist is a build failure, not a 404 discovered later.
Strip repository-reader chrome (language switcher, badges) from site projection while keeping the source usable on GitHub.
Publish raw Markdown twins at the page route plus .md, generated by the same manifest/projection pass, with frontmatter removed and links resolving file-to-file; provide an agent-facing index.
Copy referenced images beside the raw twins and ship documentation assets with the site; do not depend on the repository checkout or hotlinks.
Verify links and anchors in the source, not only through the site locale projector.
steps: Add or move the canonical document and update its owner metadata.
Update the single navigation/section source, not copied sidebar values.
Run the projector; verify route, title, chrome stripping and link targets.
Generate raw twins and asset copies from the same projection; verify a raw URL and the agent index.
Run link, anchor, navigation and build checks; fix the source, not the generated output.

enforcement.mode: automatic site build, projection and link checks
enforcement.implementation: single navigation manifest, projection pass, raw-markdown emitter, asset copy, route/anchor checks, build failure on undeclared group
enforcement.trust: Build success proves the declared routes render; it does not prove content quality or that a raw twin contains every rendered section.
enforcement.failure: An undeclared navigation group throws; a missing route, broken link or missing asset fails the build/check; raw twin drift is a generator defect.
exceptions: Frontmatter is VitePress rendering config and is intentionally dropped from raw twins.
Frozen or generated pages may have restricted navigation.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects with a documentation site plus an agent or external consumer that needs canonical Markdown.
relationships: source ownership and tiers determine what is projected
link and pairing checks remain source-level
generated pages must be deterministic before projection

migration.strategy: Keep one authored corpus, one navigation source and one projection pass; add raw twins only after routes are stable.
migration.implementation: Centralize section order/navigation, fail on undeclared groups, project without copies, emit raw page files and copied images, and add route/link checks.
migration.requiredSupport: A site generator with an explicit manifest, a route-to-file mapping, and a test that compares navigation to published routes.

positive.scenario: A new page is added to the manifest and navigation; the site builds, the route renders, and the raw .md twin resolves its images beside it.
positive.expected: Navigation, rendered route and raw twin all derive from the same source and pass link checks.

positive.scenario: A locale is missing a section placement; the build throws instead of sorting the group first.
positive.expected: The missing declaration is visible before publication.

rejection.scenario: A nav route points to a different path than the manifest publishes.
rejection.expected: The build/test fails; the 404 is not deferred to users.

rejection.scenario: A raw twin is produced by a second converter with different links.
rejection.expected: Review rejects the duplicate pipeline; raw and rendered output must share one projection.

rejection.scenario: A documentation image is hotlinked from the source repository.
rejection.expected: The asset check fails; the image is copied with the published docs.

recovery.scenario: Repository chrome leaks into rendered site pages.
recovery.expected: The projector strips it; the source retains it for GitHub readers.

recovery.scenario: A moved page leaves a stale raw URL.
recovery.expected: Redirects/aliases or updated links are added; the link check verifies the new target.

limitations: Build success is not content or translation review.
Raw twins require a route mapping that stays in sync with the site.
A site projector can still mask source-level link differences unless the source gate runs independently.

mechanisms.title: Package README, limitations and public-API documentation contracts
mechanisms.problem: Package documentation can omit durable limitations, fail to describe model-visible behavior, or let public API declarations drift from the documented type surface. Hand-written catalogs and JSDoc can omit parameters, returns or lifecycle effects, and reviewers cannot reliably notice.
triggers: A workspace package has a README or public API.
A package changes its model-visible context, token/cache behavior or lifecycle.
A public type, event payload or service method changes.
A durable consumer limitation or deferred-work item is discovered.
obligations: Every package README has a canonical Known Limitations and Deferred Work section with at least one bullet, unless an explicit no-limitations allowlist entry names that package and is removed when a limitation appears.

Model-facing or model-adjacent packages end with a canonical Model Experience section immediately before Known Limitations, with one H3 per context surface and ordered What the model sees / Token effect / KV Cache effect fields; model-agnostic packages use an explicit exclusion.
Document the machine-defined public surface: event payload parameters, public service methods, parameters and returns; stale @param names and empty tag descriptions fail.
Keep the type-equivalence catalog one-to-one with manifest entries and verified declaration structure; an unmanifested block is an orphan failure.
Chinese siblings may reuse a type block only when the whole tracked fence sequence matches order/kind/byte-exactly; otherwise they are checked independently.
Distinguish machine-checkable presence/shape from review-owned semantic accuracy and coverage.
steps: Derive the package set from manifests and require its READMEs.
Add the canonical limitations section or a justified allowlist entry.
For model-facing packages, add the Model Experience section in its canonical position and fields.
Document public events/methods and annotate returns; run the AST plus JSDoc checks.
Register catalog type blocks in the manifest; keep the Chinese side structurally equivalent.
Review coverage and meaning beyond the mechanical checks.

enforcement.mode: package-set, heading-shape, AST/JSDoc and manifest checks plus review
enforcement.implementation: verify-package-readme-limitations, model-experience contract, JSDoc completeness generator, type-equiv manifest and parser, allowlists keyed to scanned packages
enforcement.trust: Checks prove section presence/shape, documented parameters/returns and manifest correspondence; they do not prove the limitation is complete, the model-effect analysis is correct or prose is clear.
enforcement.failure: A missing/near-miss heading, empty section, stale allowlist entry, undocumented parameter/return, unmanifested type block or mismatched Chinese fence sequence fails.
exceptions: NO_LIMITATIONS and model-agnostic exclusions are explicit and must name a scanned package.
Semantic quality and limitation coverage remain reviewer-owned.

mechanisms.applicability: Monorepos or packages with public APIs and durable consumer-facing limitations, especially where model context behavior matters.
relationships: README owner and tier
catalog blocks and generated API docs share source ownership
Chinese siblings follow pairing rules

migration.strategy: Start with the package set and limitations section, then add API/JSDoc and type-catalog checks where the public surface is machine-defined.
migration.implementation: Generate the package set from manifests, add canonical headings and allowlists, parse public declarations, maintain a type-equiv manifest, and add fixture tests for near-miss headings and stale params.
migration.requiredSupport: Parser access to declarations, a package manifest scan, and reviewer ownership of coverage/meaning.

positive.scenario: A package adds a durable consumer limitation; its README gets the canonical section and one bullet, and the allowlist entry is removed if present.
positive.expected: The package-set gate finds exactly one canonical heading with a non-empty bullet.

positive.scenario: A public service method adds a parameter; the JSDoc check requires a non-empty @param and the catalog declaration remains type-equivalent.
positive.expected: The public surface is documented and the catalog is consistent.

rejection.scenario: A README uses 'Limitations' or 'Non-goals' instead of the canonical heading.
rejection.expected: The near-miss gate fails; the heading is corrected.

rejection.scenario: An empty section or stale allowlist entry remains.
rejection.expected: The gate fails on at least-one-bullet and on an allowlisted name no longer scanned.

rejection.scenario: A Chinese type block differs from the English fence sequence but is treated as reused.
rejection.expected: The independent check fails; exact order/kind/body matching is required.

recovery.scenario: A model-facing package adds a new context surface.
recovery.expected: A new H3 with the ordered effect fields is required; review verifies the analysis.

recovery.scenario: A limitation is resolved.
recovery.expected: The bullet is removed or the no-limitations allowlist is updated; the entry never silently persists.

limitations: Mechanical checks do not establish limitation completeness or model-effect correctness.
Allowlists can hide gaps if not tied to the scanned package set.
Type-equiv verifies declaration structure and JSDoc, not semantic API stability.
The core-data-structures page-scoping rule was superseded by package-anchored subsystem pages; only its type-equiv drift gate and JSDoc/README contracts transfer from that note.
mechanisms.status: current content contracts; core-data-structures page scoping superseded, type-equiv and JSDoc contracts remain

mechanisms.title: Generated references, catalogs and notices with enforced freshness
mechanisms.problem: Hand-maintained catalogs, CLI references, configuration tables, event maps and license notices drift from source. A generated file can be stale, generated in the wrong build phase, omit items, or mix runtime and build-only dependencies.
triggers: A reference describes values, defaults, APIs, events, persistence formats, notices or CLI help derived from source.
A generator input changes.
A generated page is published or read by an agent.
obligations: Generate the reference from its real source (manifests, lockfiles, declarations, actual help output, vendor metadata) rather than a second hand-written inventory.
Assert committed bytes in a test lane or run a deterministic --check; do not add a separate gate process when an existing required lane can assert the same freshness.
Name the regeneration command in the failure and list every input class that requires regeneration.
Fail loud on missing or duplicate metadata; use a reviewed override only for packages whose published metadata cannot answer, never render a blank value.

Classify dependency tiering by whether the code ships, not by manifest section; include every mountable plugin/runtime input and fail closed on a non-permissive license unless a narrow exact-identity exception is authorized.
Keep generation ordering explicit where one generated contract feeds a later build stage.
For generated references, expose a compact entry layer before exhaustive output and report retrieval size; do not apply a blanket word limit to exhaustive truth.
steps: Identify the authoritative inputs and the output bytes.
Write a deterministic generator and a check mode.
Wire freshness into an existing test lane or a required gate with the remediation command.
Add fixtures for silent-omission shapes, duplicate/conflicting entries and tiering mistakes.
Review changed generated output and exceptions; regenerate rather than hand-edit.
For large references, add an entry/index layer and a split rule based on measured lookup cost.

enforcement.mode: deterministic generator plus test-lane freshness assertion
enforcement.implementation: generator scripts, spec/`--check` comparisons, manifest/lock/vendor inputs, explicit overrides, license allowlist and exact-identity exceptions
enforcement.trust: Freshness proves committed bytes match current generation; it does not prove the generator's classification policy is correct or complete. A spec assertion is not a separate scheduler gate.
enforcement.failure: Stale bytes fail the test lane with the regeneration command; missing metadata, duplicate normalized names or conflicting versions fail generation; a non-permissive runtime dependency fails closed.
exceptions: A narrow, reviewed identity exception may cover an officially authorized payload set.
Exhaustive generated references may remain long behind a compact entry layer.
Vendored or historical evidence may be excluded by ownership rules.

mechanisms.applicability: Any project with machine-derivable reference data, especially licenses, CLI help, config defaults and generated API catalogs.
relationships: generated API/type catalogs share declaration sources
generated pages still need an owner and entry layer
dependency classification and lockfiles feed notices

migration.strategy: Pick one high-drift reference, generate it from source, and assert its bytes in an existing required lane.
migration.implementation: Create the generator and check, add input-completeness fixtures, document the regen command, and add overrides/license policy only as needed.
migration.requiredSupport: Access to installed dependency metadata and lockfiles, a deterministic environment, and an existing test lane or gate.

positive.scenario: A dependency is added and the notices generator is run; the test lane finds committed bytes current; removing the generated row fails with the exact command.
positive.expected: Freshness is enforced without a new CI step.

positive.scenario: Configuration defaults change and the generated catalog check fails, naming regeneration.
positive.expected: The committed catalog is updated by the generator, not hand-edited.

rejection.scenario: A package's metadata is missing; the generator fails instead of rendering a blank license.
rejection.expected: The failure names the package and the override path.

rejection.scenario: A test-support dependency is declared under dependencies; it is not disclosed as runtime.
rejection.expected: Tiering follows shipping reachability, not manifest section.

rejection.scenario: A non-permissive runtime dependency appears without authorization.
rejection.expected: Generation fails closed; a narrow exact-identity exception is required.

recovery.scenario: A generator input class is missed, so stale output survives.
recovery.expected: The failure list/fixtures are extended; the check covers that input.

recovery.scenario: A generated page grows too large for lookup.
recovery.expected: An entry layer and measured split rule are added without deleting exhaustive detail.

limitations: Freshness does not validate classification policy or legal sufficiency.
A generator can silently omit a package if input discovery is incomplete; fixtures reduce but do not eliminate this.
Entry-layer quality is proposed/partially shipped in the source, not fully verified.

mechanisms.title: Pinned package manager, strict workspace linking and shell-free re-entry
mechanisms.problem: Mixed package managers and hoisted or weakly constrained node_modules make local results differ from CI, hide undeclared dependencies and expose install lifecycle scripts. Recursive package-manager calls through a shell add quoting and Windows portability hazards.
triggers: A repository installs dependencies or runs package scripts.
A workspace package declares dependencies or adds a new member.
A script needs to re-enter the package manager from inside a package.
obligations: Pin one package manager and version through the manifest/packageManager field and provision it consistently in CI.
Use strict, isolated workspace linking so a package can import only declared dependencies and undeclared hoisting is visible.
Allow dependency lifecycle/build scripts only for an explicit allowlist; do not execute arbitrary transitive install scripts.
Validate workspace constraints (dependency sections, version ranges, forbidden runtime edges) mechanically.
Re-enter the package manager through its API or a direct executable with argument arrays, not through a shell string; preserve environment and exit behavior across platforms.
Treat a package-manager migration as a repository-wide change with lockfile, script and CI parity evidence, not a local preference.
steps: Choose the package manager and pin its version.
Configure strict linking and a build-script allowlist.
Add workspace constraint checks to CI.
Replace shell-based re-entry with shell-free invocation and test on supported platforms.
Regenerate the lockfile and verify clean install, scripts and CI parity.

enforcement.mode: manifest pin, install policy, workspace checks and CI
enforcement.implementation: packageManager pin, pnpm/action-setup or equivalent, node-linker settings, onlyBuiltDependencies allowlist, workspace constraint checker, shell-free spawn helpers
enforcement.trust: The pin and lockfile prove the resolved graph; they do not prove every dependency is trustworthy or that an allowlisted build script is safe.
enforcement.failure: An unpinned or mismatched package manager fails provisioning; an undeclared import or forbidden workspace edge fails the constraint check; a non-allowlisted build script is skipped or fails policy.
exceptions: A reviewed dependency may be allowlisted for build scripts.
A workspace may relax a constraint only with an explicit policy change and evidence.

mechanisms.applicability: Any multi-package JavaScript/TypeScript repository with CI and third-party install scripts.
relationships: choosing dependencies is distinct from how they are installed
CI must provision the same pinned manager
workspace edges encode product isolation

migration.strategy: Pin the manager, make linking strict, then add script and workspace policy.
migration.implementation: Set packageManager and CI provisioning, configure isolated linking, add an allowlist and a constraint checker, and replace shell re-entry.
migration.requiredSupport: A lockfile, CI cache/setup action and a documented install-script review path.

positive.scenario: A clean checkout installs with the pinned manager; a package importing an undeclared dependency fails; an allowlisted native package builds.
positive.expected: Resolution is reproducible and strictness exposes undeclared edges.

positive.scenario: A script re-enters the manager from a package and works on Windows and POSIX without shell quoting.
positive.expected: The shell-free invocation preserves arguments and exit status.

rejection.scenario: A contributor uses a different manager version.
rejection.expected: Provisioning fails or the lockfile changes, and CI rejects the mismatch.

rejection.scenario: A transitive dependency adds an install script not on the allowlist.
rejection.expected: The script does not run; review decides whether to allow it.

rejection.scenario: A workspace package adds a forbidden runtime edge.
rejection.expected: The constraint checker fails.

recovery.scenario: A migration to a new manager is needed.
recovery.expected: The change includes lockfile, scripts, CI provisioning and clean-install evidence, not just a local command.

recovery.scenario: An allowlisted build script changes behavior.
recovery.expected: Review and a lockfile update are required; the allowlist is not a blanket trust grant.

limitations: Lockfiles and pins do not establish supply-chain trust.
Strictness can expose many pre-existing undeclared imports during adoption.
The source's specific pnpm/Yarn trade-offs are project-dependent.

mechanisms.title: Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling standard concerns
mechanisms.problem: Hand-rolled parsers, retry loops, glob matchers and lockfile handling duplicate well-maintained libraries, accumulate subtle edge cases and shift maintenance onto the product. Conversely, an unvetted dependency can add supply-chain, license and runtime weight.
triggers: A standard concern appears: parsing, globbing, retries, locking, schema validation, CLI handling, HTTP, file watching.
A new dependency is proposed or an existing one is considered for removal.
A hand-rolled helper grows beyond a narrow local need.
obligations: Use a maintained, appropriate dependency for a standard concern instead of hand-rolling it, unless a documented constraint makes the dependency unsuitable.

A swap must produce net deletion of real owned code (implementation plus dedicated tests and docs), not hypothetical future code; a dependency that only adds capability is a feature decision, not a simplification.

Evaluate health and boundary fit: active maintenance, wide use, sensible transitive footprint, and semantics that cover the actual contract; residual semantics still hand-rolled around the package count against the swap.
Do not reopen a recorded design seam (for example a schema standard, vendored source or twin adapters) merely by citing the prefer-dependencies policy; beat the recorded rationale.

Record a dependency-swap proposal as a proposed/simplification note with the candidate package, deletable surface, residual semantics and supply-chain considerations. A util group's zero-dependency charter constrains harness dependencies, not external packages that simplify the code.
Pin and lock the dependency; review install scripts and supply-chain surface. Do not add a dependency for a trivial one-liner or to avoid a small adapter; document the judgment.
When removing a dependency, verify that the replacement preserves behavior and does not increase risk.
steps: Identify the standard concern, the owned implementation and the candidate package.
Check net deletion (implementation, dedicated tests and docs), health, boundary fit and residual semantics; compare against recorded seams.
Record the swap proposal and its supply-chain considerations.
Add the dependency with a lockfile update and any install-script policy.
Use it behind a narrow local interface if replacement is plausible.
Revisit when the dependency becomes unmaintained or its risk changes.

enforcement.mode: review plus dependency policy and lockfile
enforcement.implementation: dependency review checklist, lockfile, license/size/security checks, install-script allowlist
enforcement.trust: Review and metadata checks reduce risk; they do not prove the dependency is secure or maintained indefinitely.
enforcement.failure: An unjustified hand-rolled standard implementation or an unvetted dependency is a review finding; a vulnerable or non-permissive dependency fails policy.
exceptions: A documented constraint (platform, size, license, API) may justify hand-rolling a narrow piece.
A temporary local helper may precede extracting a dependency.

mechanisms.applicability: Projects deciding whether to implement or import standard functionality, especially in agent-maintained codebases.
relationships: installation and lockfile mechanics
dependency metadata feeds notices
the choice needs an evidence record

migration.strategy: Adopt a review question and a dependency checklist; do not mandate dependencies mechanically.
migration.implementation: Add a PR/review prompt, a lockfile and license check, and a short record for exceptions.
migration.requiredSupport: Dependency metadata and a reviewer able to assess risk.

positive.scenario: A contributor needs glob matching and selects a maintained library, records alternatives and adds it with a lockfile.
positive.expected: The choice is reviewable and the dependency is pinned.

positive.scenario: A hand-rolled retry helper is replaced by a maintained retry library behind a local adapter.
positive.expected: Behavior is preserved and the maintenance burden is reduced.

rejection.scenario: A new dependency is added without license or install-script review.
rejection.expected: Review rejects it until the metadata and scripts are checked.

rejection.scenario: A trivial one-line helper is replaced by a large dependency.
rejection.expected: Review rejects the unnecessary weight unless a documented constraint justifies it.

recovery.scenario: A dependency becomes unmaintained or vulnerable.
recovery.expected: The owner re-evaluates, patches, replaces or documents the accepted risk.

recovery.scenario: A replacement dependency changes behavior.
recovery.expected: Tests and compatibility evidence are required before removal of the old path.

limitations: The source's preference is a default, not a universal rule; project constraints can justify hand-rolling.
Review cannot guarantee long-term maintenance or security.
Dependency weight, ecosystem fit and net deletion are judgment calls.
The source defers advisory scanning and update cadence to a separate supply-chain proposal.

mechanisms.title: Default-product isolation, product-use classification and optional bundles
mechanisms.problem: An installation dependency can remain dormant indefinitely, experimental code can leak into the default product, and feature plugins can turn ordinary value imports into synchronous module-ordering constraints. Conversely, deployment-configured providers and embedding SDKs can have a real maintained role without appearing in the default GUI.
triggers: A package or experimental capability is added to installation/runtime dependencies.
A shipped profile, preset, dynamic mount or optional bundle changes.
A Client feature plugin imports from another feature plugin.
A package has no obvious default consumer.
obligations: Keep every experimental package outside the default product's runtime dependency graph; reject runtime imports, shipped compositions, presets and default templates that name it.

For an installation-shipped optional bundle, declare it in one typed launcher list, require a runtime dependency of the CLI app with the bundle patch declaration, and require that no shipped template selects it.
Include every mountable plugin in runtime dependency disclosure even when no default assembly imports it; under-disclosure is the costly direction.

Require nonexperimental packages to have effective product use or an explicit, reviewed classification (optional integration, SDK, build/test tool, distribution package, declaration-only infrastructure).

Compute effective use from shipped profiles, preset children, runtime source imports and explicit dynamic mounts; preserve disabled groups/Includes and apply patches; manifest dependencies and type-only references do not count.

Classify every Client cross-package reference: delete unused/forwarding values, import types as types, use an injected service for behavior, and do not declare a runtime external value edge between feature plugins.
Keep optional-bundle reachability separate from default reachability and keep experimental maturity separate from installation/selection.
steps: Classify the package's role and intended consumers.
Place experimental code outside default runtime edges; add an optional bundle only through the typed launcher list.
Run the isolation/product-use gates against the effective composition, not just manifests.
For Client imports, choose deletion, type-only import, injected service or a shared declaration owner.
Record exceptions with their maintained role and review them when the composition changes.

enforcement.mode: static dependency/composition checks plus package policy review
enforcement.implementation: default-product isolation traversal, optional-bundle allowlist and edge skips, product-use checker, workspace constraints, client external-edge classification
enforcement.trust: The checks prove declared and statically reachable edges; they cannot prove a dynamically mounted capability is never used, and an allowlist can be stale.
enforcement.failure: An experimental import/composition, an unlisted experimental dependency, an unreviewed dormant package, a forbidden client external edge or a listed bundle missing its runtime dependency fails.
exceptions: A listed optional bundle's dependency edge is skipped from the default product while its import/composition/template use remains forbidden.
A reviewed package policy entry records a non-default role.
On-demand native bundles may have a separate costly-runtime exception.

mechanisms.applicability: Products with experimental or optional capabilities, a default composition, and multiple package owners.
relationships: workspace edges and constraint checks
runtime payload disclosure and optional bundles
notices include mountable runtime plugins

migration.strategy: Define the default product and its allowed edges first, then add optional/exception mechanisms and product-use classification.
migration.implementation: Add an isolation traversal, a typed optional-bundle list with gate skips, a package policy file, and a product-use checker over effective profiles; add tests for disabled subtrees and ineffective patches.
migration.requiredSupport: A composition/manifest representation, static analysis of imports and mounts, and owners for package policy exceptions.

positive.scenario: An experimental package is added as an optional bundle; it is downloaded but not mounted by any default profile, and the isolation gate accepts only the declared dependency edge.
positive.expected: The package is inactive by default and still disclosed as runtime.

positive.scenario: A nonexperimental package has a runtime import from a shipped profile; the product-use checker reports use.
positive.expected: The package has an effective consumer and no exception is needed.

rejection.scenario: An experimental plugin adds a runtime import to a default entry or a default template selects it.
rejection.expected: The isolation gate fails; the feature cannot leak into the default product.

rejection.scenario: A dormant package is added with a policy exception that does not record a role.
rejection.expected: The policy check fails; the entry must record a maintained role.

rejection.scenario: A Client feature plugin imports a runtime value from another feature plugin.
