rejection.expected: Review rejects it; the token table owns dark values.

recovery.scenario: The RFC conflicts with the living spec.
recovery.expected: The living spec is authoritative for values; the RFC is updated only for framework-level change.

recovery.scenario: A deviation is no longer needed.
recovery.expected: The table entry and code are cleaned together.

limitations: The source's specific visual baseline and token names are project-specific.
The checklist cannot prove accessibility or aesthetic quality.
Deviation records can accumulate without periodic review.
The archived note's two-layer token table and global.css home are superseded; only its framework rulings and process remain current, and the later token system is outside this partition.
mechanisms.status: archived; framework rulings remain, two-layer token table superseded by 2026-07-22 update

mechanisms.title: Checked-in public API reports (deferred proposal)
mechanisms.problem: Public API changes are invisible: nothing makes 'this commit changed the public API' an explicit, reviewable fact, and a reviewer reading a source diff can miss an exported type gaining a field or a signature shift.
triggers: Packages are published or consumed externally and public API stability matters.
A reviewer must detect exported-surface changes rather than only source edits.
obligations: Generate a checked-in public API report per package from declarations, using api-extractor or a normalized declaration dump.
Fail CI when regeneration differs from the committed report.
Make every public API change appear as a report diff line in review.
Choose the lighter mechanism if the heavier dependency is not justified, but preserve the checked-in, diffable report shape.
steps: Decide whether packages are externally consumed and stable enough to justify the maintenance burden.
Generate etc/<pkg>.api.md or an equivalent normalized report.
Add a CI regeneration comparison.
Review report diffs with API changes.

enforcement.mode: proposed, deferred; would be automatic regeneration comparison
enforcement.implementation: none in the source at this commit; proposal only (api-extractor or tsc --emitDeclarationOnly plus normalized dump)
enforcement.trust: A report diff would prove declaration-surface change, not that the change is compatible or intentional. The proposal is not a current guarantee.
enforcement.failure: If implemented, stale reports would fail CI; currently there is no such gate.
exceptions: The source deferred the proposal for an internal monorepo where reviewers already see source diffs and the dependency/format burden was high.

mechanisms.applicability: External or published packages where public API compatibility is a real contract. Not activated merely because packages exist internally.
relationships: same checked-in/generated freshness pattern
public API documentation
external publication is the reactivation trigger

migration.strategy: Do not activate automatically; preserve the proposal and reactivate when packages become externally published or API compatibility becomes a reviewed contract.
migration.implementation: If triggered, choose api-extractor or a normalized declaration dump, commit reports, and add a CI regeneration diff.
migration.requiredSupport: A stable declaration emitter/report format, checked-in reports and a CI comparison.

positive.scenario: An exported type gains a field; regeneration changes the checked-in report and CI fails until the report is committed.
positive.expected: The API change is visible as a report diff line.

positive.scenario: A compatible refactor leaves declaration output unchanged; the report is unchanged and CI passes.
positive.expected: The report tracks the declaration surface, not arbitrary source edits.

rejection.scenario: A report is hand-edited while declarations are unchanged.
rejection.expected: CI regeneration comparison fails; the report must be generated.

rejection.scenario: The report format changes on a compiler upgrade.
rejection.expected: The maintenance cost is handled explicitly; a stable format or migration is required.

recovery.scenario: The repository remains internal or unpublished.
recovery.expected: The proposal stays deferred; no gate is claimed.

limitations: The mechanism is proposed and deferred, not implemented at the fixed commit.
The source cites a heavy/finicky dependency and report-format churn.
It does not prove semantic compatibility, only declaration-surface difference.
mechanisms.status: proposed-deferred; no active gate at the source commit

mechanisms.title: Retire temporary migration commands after live evidence
mechanisms.problem: A temporary writer can remain indefinitely beside a permanent read-only check, creating a second apparent maintenance path. Removing it too early can strand branches with large manual conflicts.
triggers: A transition introduced a temporary mutation command alongside permanent enforcement.
The migration window may have closed.
Branches still carry pre-transition data.
obligations: Remove the temporary command only after a live inventory confirms no open PR still needs it; elapsed time is not evidence.
Keep the permanent canonicalizer, its unit tests and the read-only snapshot/gate; only the branch-facing writer is temporary.
Remove the root command, branch-convergence links, docs and command-specific diagnostics in the same change; replace remediation with command-independent canonical-layout guidance.
Before removal, each affected branch merges current main, runs the migrator once, commits the fixture-only rewrite separately and verifies the repository-wide check.
Update current documentation to describe only the permanent default and enforcement.
steps: Inventory open PRs for data needing the temporary command.
Confirm the permanent check covers future data and fails on noncanonical input.
Give affected branches a merge/run/commit/verify procedure.
Remove the CLI, root command, links and command-specific diagnostic.
Run the remaining permanent checks and document the final state.

enforcement.mode: proposed transition process; would rely on live inventory and the permanent check
enforcement.implementation: none executed at this commit; proposal defines the removal set and acceptance
enforcement.trust: A live PR inventory proves the known migration set; it cannot prove an unopened branch has no need. The permanent snapshot proves canonical layout, not migration completeness.
enforcement.failure: Removal without a live inventory risks stranded branches; retaining the command leaves two maintenance paths; removing the canonicalizer would remove enforcement.
exceptions: Closed or superseded branches need no migration.
Retaining the command longer is lower operational cost but obscures the permanent mechanism.

mechanisms.applicability: Any temporary migration command that coexists with a permanent read-only gate. The source's packed-session fixture is one instance.
relationships: temporary mechanisms must not become permanent authorities
the permanent check must remain
removal must include links and diagnostics, not only the CLI

migration.strategy: Keep the permanent canonicalizer; remove only the branch-facing writer after live evidence and with a branch procedure.
migration.implementation: Inventory open PRs, publish the convergence procedure, remove command/root script/links/diagnostic, and retain/verify the snapshot check.
migration.requiredSupport: PR inventory access, the permanent canonicalizer, and a documented branch convergence path.

positive.scenario: A live inventory shows no open branch needs the migrator; the CLI and links are removed, the snapshot check remains and passes.
positive.expected: Only the temporary mechanism disappears.

positive.scenario: An affected branch merges main, runs the migrator once and verifies the canonical snapshot.
positive.expected: The branch converges without re-recording data.

rejection.scenario: The command is removed without checking open PRs.
rejection.expected: The process rejects the removal as unsupported by live evidence.

rejection.scenario: The canonicalizer is removed with the CLI.
rejection.expected: The permanent enforcement is lost; removal is rejected.

rejection.scenario: A stale command-specific diagnostic remains.
rejection.expected: The same-change cleanup acceptance fails.

recovery.scenario: A closed/superseded branch still has old data.
recovery.expected: It needs no migration and is not counted.

recovery.scenario: A branch was missed.
recovery.expected: The live-inventory limitation is acknowledged; the branch uses the documented manual/regeneration path or the command is restored.

limitations: Proposed, not executed at the fixed commit.
A live inventory can miss unopened work.
The source's fixture format and command names are product-specific.
mechanisms.status: proposed; removal not executed at the source commit

mechanisms.title: Audience-first documentation quality criteria (partially shipped proposal)
mechanisms.problem: A documentation system can pass placement, freshness, link, bilingual and source-equivalence checks while still failing readers: prose names removed mechanisms, no one owns the current fact, success is implicit, generated accuracy is conflated with retrieval quality, and the standing standard has no room for new rules.
triggers: Documentation is technically valid but a reader cannot complete a task or find one answer.
A generated reference overwhelms retrieval or a page dominates agent context.
A standing documentation standard is at its budget ceiling.
A package README entry or summary lacks audience/outcome information.
obligations: Define brief, intuitive, friendly, accurate and agent-readable as reviewable outcomes by document job, not as universal slogans.

Brief: the common path contains only facts needed for the outcome; exhaustive contracts remain behind direct links or generated detail; never delete required behavior, failures, ownership or limitations.
Intuitive: establish the reader's starting state, introduce prerequisites before dependent concepts, offer one obvious next action, use the terms readers search for.
Friendly: let readers recognize success, understand material risk before acting, recover from likely failure and reach the next depth without unrelated architecture.

Accurate: every durable claim has one owner and a risk-appropriate verification path; generated facts derive from source; hand-written workflow values link/consume their owner instead of copying enums and paths.
Agent-readable: headings, anchors, terminology, ownership and current-versus-proposed status make the needed section retrievable without loading the corpus or reconstructing review history.
Require an explicit entry paragraph/Summary, structure and outcome for each document job; use metadata only when a retrieval/template/bilingual consumer uses it.
For generated references, provide a compact scope/index/entry layer before exhaustive output, report retrieval size, and split by a stable source domain when measured lookup cost warrants it.
Make the sidecar the single consistency record until its replacement passes verifier, merge-driver, recovery, generated-region and archive checks.
Keep slices independently reviewable and measure before corpus-wide structural change.
steps: Classify the document job and state its primary outcome and required entry information.
Add the canonical Summary/entry layer and structure; keep exact contracts in owning sections.
Define ownership and verification for each durable claim; link workflow values.
Prototype generated entry/detail separation on one large catalog and one mixed page.
Measure lookup steps, generated diff size, build time, route stability and agent context before broader splitting.
Migrate one coherent topic at a time with atomic link/navigation repair.

enforcement.mode: partially shipped via dsh-doc and test:docs; remaining criteria are proposed
enforcement.implementation: canonical quality reference, package README metadata/Summary checks, document-job table, generated-reference prototype; slices 1-3 shipped in source, 4-5 open
enforcement.trust: Metadata/Summary/line-alignment checks prove shape, not reader success. The audit uses repository structure and representative pages, not user research. The proposal explicitly does not yet prove the broad corpus change.
enforcement.failure: A package Summary over the limit fails the focused check; a missing canonical quality reference or budget headroom is a review finding; generated-reference split without measured evidence is rejected.
exceptions: Format-owned notes, postmortems, generated fragments and machine files keep their skeletons.
Exhaustive references can remain long behind an entry layer.
Relative links remain until a root-relative form passes GitHub/site/anchor checks.

mechanisms.applicability: Documentation systems with multiple audiences and generated references. The source states slices 1-3 shipped; slices 4-5 and full corpus-wide application remain proposed.
relationships: tiers and budgets are the substrate
package README sections and summaries
entry/detail layering for generated pages

migration.strategy: Adopt the five definitions and job table first, prototype one package README and one generated page, then migrate only after measured evidence.
migration.implementation: Create one canonical quality reference, add package README metadata/Summary checks, keep sidecars until replacement is proven, and prototype entry/detail separation.
migration.requiredSupport: dsh-doc or equivalent standard, focused metadata/summary/link tests, and real reader-task validation before broad rollout.

positive.scenario: A package README summary states the reader-visible capability in 100 words and links the canonical quality reference; the focused check passes.
positive.expected: The entry layer is compact and the detailed contracts remain in owning sections.

positive.scenario: A generated catalog gains a scope/index layer and reports page/entry/heading counts; a representative lookup uses fewer steps without lost facts.
positive.expected: Retrieval improves while exhaustive truth and determinism remain.

rejection.scenario: A page is technically valid but names a removed sidebar/section owner.
rejection.expected: The semantic-currency review catches it; a gate alone does not prove the prose current.

rejection.scenario: A metadata field has no retrieval/template/bilingual consumer.
rejection.expected: It is rejected as boilerplate.

rejection.scenario: A generated reference is split by arbitrary word count.
rejection.expected: Review rejects it; splits follow a stable source domain and measured lookup cost.

recovery.scenario: A proposed slice is not shipped.
recovery.expected: It is recorded as open/proposed, not claimed as an active guarantee.

recovery.scenario: Exact line alignment forces unnatural translation.
recovery.expected: Review revises both sides to protect meaning rather than weakening one side.

limitations: Slices 1-3 shipped; slices 4-5 and full corpus application remain open.
The audit is not user research.
Metadata can become boilerplate; sentence limits can fragment explanations.
Reader success is not automatically proven by the focused checks.
mechanisms.status: proposed; slices 1-3 shipped, slices 4-5 and corpus-wide adoption open
